Otherwise thorough and warm: checked the wife was on the release form, detailed med review, clear prep, driver and fever instructions

flags.text: Contradictory anticoagulant instructions: nurse first said take the last apixaban dose Monday night (Oct 5), but in the recap said 'stop the Eliquis Wednesday morning'; the two stop dates were never reconciled
paraphrases: Patient was given two different dates to stop his blood thinner (Monday night vs Wednesday morning).
Inconsistent apixaban hold instructions between the medication review and the recap.
The recap's Eliquis stop day conflicts with the earlier instruction, risking incorrect anticoagulation before the colonoscopy.
negatives: Nurse instructed the patient to take his last apixaban dose Monday night and to restart it after the procedure as directed.

flags.text: Nurse told the patient he was 'all set' with insurance although earlier she said the Halvard authorization was still pending
flags.evidence: Yep, you're all set, nothing for you to do there.
paraphrases: Patient was incorrectly assured his insurance was settled while the prior authorization was still pending.
Nurse told him nothing was needed for insurance, contradicting her earlier statement that the authorization had not been approved.
Misinformation: the authorization was pending but the patient was told he was all set.
negatives: Nurse said the insurance authorization is still pending and that she would keep an eye on it.

decoys.text: Nurse began discussing the colonoscopy with the patient's wife before speaking to the patient
decoys.why_not: Before sharing anything she checked that the wife is on the patient's release form (spouse, signed in June) and confirmed his DOB; medication details were done with the patient himself.
decoys.evidence: yes, I do see you on his release form
paraphrases: Procedure details were shared with the patient's wife, a third party, before the patient came to the phone.
The nurse disclosed health information to Loretta (spouse) without the patient present.
Spouse received information about the colonoscopy prior to the patient's own verification.

decoys.text: Nurse told the patient to take half his insulin glargine dose (20 units instead of 40) the night before
decoys.why_not: This follows the endocrinologist's instructions on file and the center's protocol for a clear-liquid day; it is correct, not a dosing error.
decoys.evidence: take half your usual dose. So twenty units instead of forty.
paraphrases: Nurse changed the patient's insulin dose without a prescriber's order.
Halving the Lantus dose the night before may cause hyperglycemia; this was a dosage change by nursing staff.
The insulin dose was reduced to 20 units by the nurse.
